_note: 🧠 Câu suy luận cho bài luyện Đọc / Nghe B1, B2 (v103, Claude soạn, chưa giáo viên kiểm): điều bài không nói thẳng (thái độ, mục đích, ý ngầm). Thêm vào qs của bài với sl: 1 (tính vào 🔍 chi tiết, đo trên bài mới). C1, C2 đã có câu suy luận / thái độ trong bài.

doc-b1-1.q: What does the text suggest was Hoa's main problem at first?
doc-b1-1.a: Work and home life were not separated.
w: She had too little work to do.
Her company wanted her back in the office.

doc-b1-2.q: What can we infer about the car park during the building work?
doc-b1-2.a: It may be hard to find a space.
w: It will be closed for four weeks.
Members will have to pay to use it.

doc-b1-3.q: What kind of person is Tuan, according to the story?
w: Lucky and rich.
Clever but lazy.

doc-b1-4.q: What is the head teacher's position at the moment?
doc-b1-4.a: Undecided: the school wants to hear more views first.
w: The head teacher agrees with Linh.
The school has already stopped uniforms.

doc-b1-5.q: What does the story suggest about job interviews?
doc-b1-5.a: Being honest about a mistake can help you.
w: You should never talk about your mistakes.
Arriving on time is not important.

doc-b1-6.q: What does the writer think about deposit schemes?
w: They are too expensive to run.
They have not been tried anywhere yet.

doc-b2-1.q: What does Thu Trang's comment suggest about the company before the change?
doc-b2-1.a: Many meetings were not really necessary.
w: Staff often worked at weekends.
Projects were usually finished early.

doc-b2-2.q: What does the writer imply about people who say they are 'bad with names'?
doc-b2-2.a: They usually do not pay enough attention when they first hear a name.
w: They have a serious memory problem.
They simply meet too many people.

doc-b2-3.q: What does 'He tells everyone it was his idea' suggest?
doc-b2-3.a: Her father is now proud of her decision.
w: Her father planned the gap year himself.
Her father is still angry with her.

doc-b2-4.q: Why does the writer mention Seoul and Ho Chi Minh City?
doc-b2-4.a: To show that the trend is happening in many places.
w: To compare prices in the two cities.
Because board games were invented there.

doc-b2-5.q: What is the writer's attitude to the council's explanation?
doc-b2-5.a: He doubts that it is completely true.
w: He fully agrees with it.
He thinks every tree really was dangerous.

doc-b2-6.q: Why does the writer say 'Phones are not completely innocent'?
doc-b2-6.a: Phones make the problem worse, even though biology is the main cause.
w: Phones are the only reason teenagers sleep late.
Phones help teenagers fall asleep faster.

ng-b1-1.q: What can we guess about the caller?
ng-b1-1.a: The caller wants to spend as little money as possible.
w: The caller is travelling with a family.
The caller has stayed at the hostel before.

ng-b1-2.q: What can we infer about the sports hall?
ng-b1-2.a: It has less space than the park.
w: Anyone can go in without a ticket.
It has no car park.

ng-b1-3.q: How does Nam probably feel at the end of the conversation?
ng-b1-3.a: Happy to try the cooking class.
w: Worried about his brother's knee.
Annoyed that his friend asked him.

ng-b1-4.q: What is the main purpose of Thu's talk?
ng-b1-4.a: To explain what will happen during the visit.
w: To sell tickets for the film.
To teach the full history of the port.

ng-b1-5.q: What does the doctor's advice suggest about the patient's problem?
ng-b1-5.a: It is probably caused by his habits, not by an illness.
w: It is very serious.
He needs medicine immediately.

ng-b1-6.q: What can we infer about the family before the project?
ng-b1-6.a: They did not know how much rubbish they produced.
w: They already had a compost box.
They never bought anything made of plastic.

ng-b2-1.q: What is Vu's attitude to the cable car?
ng-b2-1.a: He sees both good and bad sides.
w: He thinks it has ruined his job.
He is completely in favour of it.

ng-b2-2.q: What is the speaker's attitude to studying all night before an exam?
ng-b2-2.a: The speaker thinks it is a mistake.
w: The speaker recommends it.
The speaker thinks it makes no difference.

ng-b2-3.q: What can we infer about the man's opinion at the end?
ng-b2-3.a: He is still not fully convinced, but he might go again.
w: He has decided he loved the film.
He refuses to see it again.

ng-b2-4.q: What is the transport association's attitude?
ng-b2-4.a: Positive about the sales, but worried about charging.
w: Against electric motorbikes.
Not interested in air pollution.

ng-b2-5.q: Why does the man say 'That's what makes it so hard'?
ng-b2-5.a: His wife wants to go, but he is worried about his parents.
w: The salary in Singapore is too low.
He does not like Singapore.

ng-b2-6.q: Why does the speaker begin with 'Most people are surprised'?
ng-b2-6.a: Many people do not know how much coffee Vietnam produces.
w: Vietnamese coffee is very expensive.
Coffee only came to Vietnam recently.

doc-b1-16.q: What can we infer about the tool library?
doc-b1-16.a: It has helped people learn new skills.
w: It has made a large profit.
It is used mostly by builders.

doc-b1-17.q: What kind of person does David seem to be?
w: Strict and unfriendly.
Too busy to care about Minh.

doc-b1-18.q: How does the writer feel about the week now?
w: It was a complete waste of time.
Everyone should stop using phones.

doc-b1-19.q: What does Linh mean in her last sentence?
doc-b1-19.a: Her father now controls the price of his rice.
w: Her father works harder than before.
Her father wants to stop farming.

doc-b1-20.q: What does the expert suggest about small purchases?
doc-b1-20.a: Together they cost more than people think.
w: They are not worth writing down.
They are the reason people travel.

doc-b2-16.q: What does the frog-counter's comment suggest?
doc-b2-16.a: The project made the volunteer notice the local area.
w: The volunteer found counting frogs boring.
The pond had only recently been built.

doc-b2-17.q: Why does the writer put 'sustainable' in quotation marks?
doc-b2-17.a: To suggest the claim may not be fully true.
w: To show it is a technical term.
To show consumers invented the word.

doc-b2-18.q: What can we infer about the 'middle way'?
doc-b2-18.a: It does not fully satisfy either side.
w: It has ended the debate.
It is supported by most critics.

doc-b2-19.q: How does Hung feel about his situation?
doc-b2-19.a: He feels his work is not recognised.
w: He enjoys working while the city is quiet.
He wants to find a day job soon.

doc-b2-20.q: Why does the writer begin by asking about brushing your teeth?
doc-b2-20.a: To show how little we notice our habits.
w: To give advice about health.
To show that habits are easy to change.

ng-b1-16.q: What can we infer about the customer?
ng-b1-16.a: He would have preferred a black jacket.
w: He has never shopped there before.
He wants his money back.

ng-b1-17.q: What can we infer about the lockers?
w: They are only for members.
They are next to the café.

ng-b1-18.q: Why does the woman say 'Oh no'?
ng-b1-18.a: She is worried she will arrive too late.
w: She has forgotten her aunt's address.
She doesn't have enough money.

ng-b1-19.q: What can we infer about the price of the class?
ng-b1-19.a: Students don't need to buy any food.
w: It is cheaper for small groups.
It includes a free container.

ng-b1-20.q: What does the woman's question about rain show?
ng-b1-20.a: She is thinking about possible problems.
w: She doesn't like picnics.
She has checked the weather forecast.

ng-b2-16.q: What does the artist's advice suggest about painting without permission?
ng-b2-16.a: It may stop artists from getting more work.
w: It is the fastest way to become famous.
It is the only way to make real street art.

ng-b2-17.q: How does the speaker seem to feel about the project?
ng-b2-17.a: Positive, though aware of the difficulties.
w: Disappointed by the results.
Worried that it costs too much.

ng-b2-18.q: What can we infer about the man's study habits?
ng-b2-18.a: He has been leaving work until the last minute.
w: He has been testing himself regularly.
He has been studying with friends.

ng-b2-19.q: What can we infer about the next few years in Riverton?
w: The reservoir will soon be full.
Bottled water will be banned.

ng-b2-20.q: Why does the woman want to visit on a Friday night?
ng-b2-20.a: To find out how noisy the bar is.
w: To meet the other tenants.
Because the rent is lower at weekends.
